purpose: testing.ExecutionInfo (analysis/test/ExecutionInfo.java, starlarkbuildapi/test/ExecutionInfoApi.java): the provider constructor's BuiltinFunction binding and Dict.cast errors, the NativeInfo instance (type, dir, repr, struct fields with fresh dict projections, content equality and hashing, frozen load-time instances), dep[testing.ExecutionInfo] / `in`, attr.label(providers = [testing.ExecutionInfo]), `provides = [testing.ExecutionInfo]` (checkDeclaredProviders), rules_python 1.7.0's py_interpreter_program + precompile.bzl pattern (requirements from a string-list build setting onto an action), and a test rule's ExecutionInfo on its test action (`build`, `--nobuild`, `test`: requirements merged into the test spawn's execution info, the exec group of its owner). Motivation: @@rules_python+//tools/precompiler:precompiler blocked analysis of ~/code's //src/beyondwork.ai/tools/... (`testing.ExecutionInfo is not implemented in the native profile`).

reference.environment: env -i PATH=/usr/bin:/bin HOME/TMPDIR private LANG=C.UTF-8 LC_ALL=C.UTF-8; default registry (bcr.bazel.build); one fresh copy of the fixture workspace per case (platforms extracted from tests/fixtures/label_repo_name/platforms_archive.json)

normalization: <WS> = the case's workspace copy; <OB> = the genuine output base; <CACHE> = the native cache; elapsed times <T>. Outputs are the top-level outputs (genuine --show_result lines, bazel-bin = bazel-out/k8-fastbuild/bin; native LABEL<TAB>PATH lines below the action output root) as [mode, contents].
comparison (tests/execution_info.rs, liv: MATCH: success equal; WARNING lines equal in order; a failing case's genuine message (the `Error in <callable>: ` / `Error: ` Starlark text, else the rule error following an empty `in KIND rule L: ` line, else the first ERROR message) is contained in native stderr; built top-level outputs (path below bazel-out -> [mode, contents]) equal; `test`: the summary's target status lines and `Executed` line equal (times <T>). DECLARED_DIVERGENCE: native fails with the recorded message.
genuine_key_findings: type(testing.ExecutionInfo) is Provider (repr <function ExecutionInfo>); an instance has type ExecutionInfo, dir ["exec_group", "requirements"], repr/str `struct(exec_group = "test", requirements = {"requires-x": "1", "b": ""})` (insertion order), exec_group defaults to "test" and requirements to {}.
Each `requirements` access is a fresh mutable dict: mutating it does not change the provider.

Instances compare by content (map equality ignores order, exec_group counts; never equal to a struct) and hash consistently (usable as dict keys); one created while a .bzl loads can be returned by a rule and compares equal through a dependency.

Binding (BuiltinFunction): `in call to ExecutionInfo(), parameter 'requirements' got value of type 'list', want 'dict'` (also before the surplus-positional count and before a duplicate), `... parameter 'exec_group' ... want 'string'`, `ExecutionInfo() got unexpected keyword argument 'requirement' (did you mean 'requirements'?)`, `ExecutionInfo() accepts no more than 2 positional arguments but got 3`, `ExecutionInfo() got multiple values for argument 'requirements'`; Dict.cast: `got dict<int, string> for 'requirements', want dict<string, string>`; fields: `'ExecutionInfo' value has no field or method 'nope'`, `cannot set .requirements field of ExecutionInfo value`.

`provides = [testing.ExecutionInfo]` without returning it fails: `rule advertised the 'ExecutionInfo' provider, but this provider was not among those returned` (checkDeclaredProviders looks every advertised key up on the built target; DefaultInfo/OutputGroupInfo are always there). A dep without it in attr.label(providers = [testing.ExecutionInfo]): `'//pkg:plain' does not have mandatory providers: 'ExecutionInfo'`.
The py_interpreter_program shape (executable = False, DefaultInfo(executable = symlink)) builds; its requirements reach a run_shell action that runs the program from the exec configuration.
A test rule returning ExecutionInfo builds, also with --nobuild, whatever its exec group (the test action is created at analysis; `build` never runs it).

`test` applies its requirements to the test action (TestTargetProperties.java:115-118 puts them over the tags' execution info): requirements = {"no-sandbox": ""} runs the test spawn with the local strategy (`INFO: 7 processes: 6 internal, 2 local.` instead of `2 processwrapper-sandbox`); requirements = {"requires-network": ""} under --nosandbox_default_allow_network passes (the genuine processwrapper-sandbox never blocks the network; natively the Landlock sandbox denies the connection without the merged requirement, with `Permission denied`, and the test fails).
exec_group = "other" (declared by the rule) runs the test in that group's owner: PASSED on this host.
known_divergences: Exit codes of command-line errors are not exercised; analysis failures exit 1 on both sides.
Native prints its own result format (`LABEL\tPATH`, `bazel-rs: N actions executed ...`), no INFO lines, and Starlark errors in its own traceback format (the messages are Bazel's).
Declared divergence other_group_test: see the case.
Native needs --experimental-builtin-modules for the exec cases (the default host platform's @platforms//host); it is passed in every native case.
